precepts.text: My temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus. You see how men are received like angels.
precepts.point: How do you go about not being beguiled? If you study, you do not willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to shew thyself approved, that you will be able to withstand these men.
precepts.why:
“Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”. What does he mean by worshipping of angels? Paul shows it: “And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.”

The Galatians received Paul, a man, as an angel of God. You see how men are considered like angels. So the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18 is the worshipping of men: following man, voluntarily humbling yourself to men.

And he is not changing the subject. It goes back to verse 4, “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words”, and verse 8, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” He is on the same train of thought, repeating it again.

So when you read verse 18, it is not Michael and Uriel coming down from the heavens to talk to you. It is men that speak so well, with enticing words and the wisdom of this world, received as if they were angels of God, and people giving themselves over to them.

precepts.text: For this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. Who was under the first testament? Israel. Nail in the coffin.
precepts.point: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years; I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. Colossians 2:16: let no man judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. Ezekiel 45:17 answers both: it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings, and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths, and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and the Pharisees, whose bread and butter was people bringing animals, were trying to win the churches back to temple law, saying to hell with what Christ did. If you need an animal, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“But when the fulness of the time was come”, the time appointed of the Father, “God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.” Who did Christ come to redeem? Them that were under the law. The we is the same we of chapter 3 that were kept under the law, and the adoption pertains to Israel.

Hebrews is the nail in the coffin: “And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” Christ is the mediator of the new testament by means of his death, hanging on the cross. Redemption is the redeeming, and he died for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament.

Who was under the first testament? Israel. So those Christ redeemed are those who were under the law, the called who receive the promise of eternal inheritance: the heirs.

“And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.” When Christ died we were no longer servants but sons of the Father, and heirs through his Son.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?” We know the true God now, not a pagan one, and we are known of God because Christ died for us. Verse 3 said we were in bondage under the elements of the world; verse 9 calls them weak and beggarly elements. It is the same bondage the false brethren of chapter 2 wanted to bring us back into. So what are they?

Some say we keep saying law of sacrifice and it does not say that. But it does call it weak. “For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh”. Weak through the flesh means weak through our sin, through us.

What could the law not do? Hebrews 9:9 says the gifts and sacrifices “could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrificing of animals could not make us perfect. That is what the law could not do, and that is the weak in the weak and beggarly elements.

So God sent his own Son to do what the animals could not, and to turn back to animal sacrifice after knowing God is to desire again to be in bondage.

precepts.text: There is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof, for the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did, by the which we draw nigh unto God. Hebrews 10:1: the law, having a shadow of good things to come, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. Animal sacrifice is the weak and beggarly elements, unprofitable because we were too sinful to keep maintaining it.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Paul calls them “weak and beggarly elements”. Hebrews calls the same thing weak: “For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” The disannulling is of animal sacrifice. What made it weak and unprofitable? “For the law made nothing perfect”, including the man's conscience, “but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.” That better hope is Christ.

Hebrews 10 says it again: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” It could not make those who offered them perfect.

So the weak and beggarly elements are the sacrificing of animals. They were unprofitable because we were too sinful to keep maintaining them.

That is why verse 10 says “Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years”. Ezekiel 45:17 shows that it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. Colossians 2:16 matches it: meat, drink, holyday, new moon and sabbath days: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and Christ is the body, the sacrifice for all of those things. The Galatians were turning back to observing those days by the weak and beggarly elements.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Who was bewitching the Galatians back into bondage? “And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” After the manner of Moses, sacrifice followed circumcision, on the eighth day. To be circumcised after the manner of Moses meant going back to sacrifice.

“When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.” These men came from Judea infiltrating and causing confusion, saying you have to sacrifice.

“But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” The Pharisees came in as believers, part of the church, and were imposing that you had to sacrifice according to the manner of Moses. These are the same false brethren brought in unawares that Galatians addresses, who came in privily to spy out our liberty and bring us into bondage.

As the movement grew, the Pharisees went into the churches to win them back to temple law. Paul said he profited in the Jews' religion; people bringing animals was their bread and butter. They were saying to hell with what Christ did, you need an animal for atonement. Paul's answer: if you do, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

precepts.text: Almost all things are by the law purged with blood. Almost, not all, so stop saying blood sacrifice; the heathen will come with that. Leviticus 5:11-12: if he be not able to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering, with no oil or frankincense, and the priest burns a memorial of it. Sirach 35:1-3: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough; he that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; to depart from wickedness is pleasing to the Lord, and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation. Israel never got there; it thought it could sin and sacrifice endlessly, and the Lord said enough.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“And almost all things are by the law purged with blood”. Almost, not all. So be mindful of always saying blood sacrifice, because the heathen are going to come with that. Not every sin offering was blood, because some among us were poor and could not bring a blood sacrifice.

Leviticus shows it: “But if he be not able to bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he that sinned shall bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense thereon: for it is a sin offering.” The priest took his handful of it as a memorial and burned it on the altar.

And the main example was obedience: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering. He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise. To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” A propitiation is reconciliation. When you depart from sin and keep God's commandments, that is sacrifice enough.

Israel never got there. Israel thought, I can sin all I want and sacrifice all I want, and I'm good. We were children under the schoolmaster, sacrificing and sinning again, going into slavery and out and back again. The Lord said enough of that, and sent his Son. That is why turning back to the weak and beggarly elements is turning back to bondage.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” We do not understand the power we have, or where we came from. Paul tells us: “But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.”

A lot of times we read that and it goes over our heads, but pay attention to the wording. Jerusalem which is above is the mother of us all, meaning we all came from there. That is where we came from. There are different levels of understanding to these scriptures.

So when Christ says he is not of this world, and tells us we are not of this world and to love not the world, understand what he is saying. When the Bible says we are pilgrims and strangers on this earth, understand what it is saying. And when it says that if we had been mindful of whence we came, we might have had opportunity to return, understand what it is saying.

We are the sons of God cast down to the nether parts of the earth, walking in darkness and dying like men, but our mother is the Jerusalem above. You have to believe these things and understand them, because that is who you are.

precepts.text: Jerusalem is free and is the mother of us all. If I don't remember that and glorify these other lands, I'm not in the divine will of God.
precepts.point: We have to prefer Jerusalem above our chief joy. That's why Paul in the book of Hebrews says we have a country that we're going back to, and no Christian acknowledges that.

precepts.text: Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all: Jerusalem is the motherland, and another name for Jerusalem is Zion.
precepts.point: You ever hear of the tree, the weeping willow? A very sad tree; the leaves thereof hang down like it's in a weeping state. We hanged our harps upon it because we had no more joy, no more happiness.

precepts.text: God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law.
precepts.point: When eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus. He was born under the law and everything done for him was done after the law.

note.label: Luke 2: The Birth at Bethlehem and the Child in the Temple

precepts.why:
Paul writes that “when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.”

He was made under the law, and everything done for him was done after the law: the circumcising of the child when eight days were accomplished is the law being kept on him.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

precepts.why: What is the adoption? “God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law”. That’s not all nations on the planet Earth. All nations were not under the law of God; he gave the law to Moses, who gave it to the 12 tribes of Israel, “that we might receive the adoption of sons.” So that only pertains to the 12 tribes of Israel.

All the schools that come out of that branch out of One West teach the New Covenant under Christ, so where do we get a sect of brothers who say yahawashi but say we’re under the old covenant? “Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch”: maybe their blind leaders led them down that path. So we’re going to reach our hands into the pit and help pull out our blind brothers.

“And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not”. “I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight”: hopefully that light is made straight in the dark path our brothers are walking down, and Christ is illuminated, and they come to understand Christ and the New Covenant and remove the veil from their face.

Where did we read about the weakness and unprofitableness earlier? A brother behind the camera, without his Bible open, answered Galatians; he’s been on point all night, and that makes my teeth white, like Bishop says. “How turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements”: the weak and beggarly elements are the same weakness and unprofitableness here in Hebrews 7:18, the law of animal sacrifice.

“But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law”. God sent forth Christ, made of a woman: he came just the way we came. Made under the law: circumcised on the eighth day, keeping the passover, the dedication and all the feast days.

“To redeem them that were under the law”. This shows who redemption is for, and this is for you dumb Christians: it is for those that were under the law. Were all nations under the law? No. Were the Chinese under the law? Was Esau under the law? Never. Christ came and died for those under the law because they broke the law, the curses came upon them, they sold themselves for nought and were scattered throughout the four corners of the earth in slavery. So Christ died and paid that price to get them out, to redeem us from under the curse of the law, which is slavery.

“That we might receive the adoption of sons”: so that now we might be the sons of God.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why: “Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?” We become the enemies of our people because we tell them the laws of God. Imagine if they had been rebuked from the scriptures. We are a hateful people that hate the word of God.

points: Now comes the question: if we as a people are the Israelites, how is it that you say Africa is not our homeland?

Paul is telling the Galatians: you didn't reject me when I was going through all my trials. I was transparent and telling you what I struggled with, and you didn't go against me.
But received me as an angel of God. So it's not talking about literal angels. It's talking about the leaders. Paul is referring to himself as an angel.

For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman: right. So Abraham had two sons. It says one by a bondmaid and the other by a free woman. Who is the son by a bondmaid?
the one by a bondmaid: the one by a bondmaid, which was Ishmael, Hagar's son.
the other by a freewoman: so who's the free woman?
the one by a bondmaid: Hagar.
the other by a freewoman: so the other he had by a free woman, which was who? Sarah was the mother and Isaac was the son.

but he of the freewoman was by promise: he that was born from Sarah, was by promise. Because the Lord said at this set time next year, she's going to have your son. It is going to happen. This is a promise. Remember, he said kings of people shall come out of her and all that.
But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh: that's Ishmael.
but he of the freewoman was by promise: that's Isaac. Watch this.

Which things are an allegory: so now, which goes back to the topic of the lesson. These things, that history, everything that happened in Genesis that we read in chapter 16, chapter 17, Hagar having Ishmael and the Lord promising Sarah to have Isaac, that was an allegory.
for these are the two covenants: so those things, that history, represents the two covenants.
